Gap Register.Gap within selected corpus: Synchronized packets + independent process truth + operator intent
Gap Register.Current evidence / partial coverage: SWaT offers packet/process pairs behind access restrictions; GRFICS can generate a joint record; other datasets omit parts
Gap Register.Why it matters: A decoded write does not establish the physical consequence or whether it was authorized
Gap Register.Action to close gap: Instrument one canonical simulator with separate state, controller readings, HMI events and exact event labels
Gap Register.Validation evidence required: Common timebase; tag map; simulator state; captures; operator/maintenance log; honest truth provenance

Gap Register.Gap within selected corpus: Benign rare operations and equipment faults
Gap Register.Current evidence / partial coverage: IEC collection includes legitimate electrical disturbances; conference traffic is not clean operational labeling
Gap Register.Why it matters: Maintenance, restart, link failure and sensor failure can resemble attacks
Gap Register.Action to close gap: Generate labeled startup, shutdown, maintenance, device fault and communication-loss scenarios alongside attacks
Gap Register.Validation evidence required: Same process under benign and malicious cases; documented authorization and outcomes

Gap Register.Gap within selected corpus: EtherNet/IP explicit messaging versus cyclic I/O
Gap Register.Current evidence / partial coverage: SWaT/WADI document EtherNet/IP but exact release capture mix not decoded; Conpot provides service emulation
Gap Register.Why it matters: Service support alone does not establish authentic cyclic I/O timing or process coupling
Gap Register.Action to close gap: Inspect permitted traces and create explicit-message plus cyclic-I/O benchmark scenarios where supported
Gap Register.Validation evidence required: Decoded services, connection parameters, capture vantage and measured cadence

Gap Register.Gap within selected corpus: PROFINET real-time and discovery / alarm traffic
Gap Register.Current evidence / partial coverage: No validated PROFINET packet corpus identified in this selected set; S7comm does not imply PROFINET coverage
Gap Register.Why it matters: Controller application traffic and real-time I/O teach different communication patterns
Gap Register.Action to close gap: Add a documented isolated controller / I/O capture or a separately licensed dataset
Gap Register.Validation evidence required: Layer-2 dissections, topology, update intervals, alarms and benign operational labels

Gap Register.Gap within selected corpus: DNP3 and IEC 60870-5-104 with physical context
Gap Register.Current evidence / partial coverage: 4SICS inventories DNP3 services; Conpot documents IEC 104 emulation; neither establishes rich labeled process truth
Gap Register.Why it matters: Utility event reporting and control sequences require context beyond port discovery
Gap Register.Action to close gap: Seek a permitted utility dataset or build a controlled outstation/process simulation
Gap Register.Validation evidence required: Actual protocol objects/events, synchronized physical state and operator authorization

Gap Register.Gap within selected corpus: OPC UA subscriptions and secure modes
Gap Register.Current evidence / partial coverage: OpenPLC lists an OPC UA plugin; HAI uses acquisition through an OPC UA gateway but distributes CSV
Gap Register.Why it matters: Process data does not expose session, subscription or encrypted-traffic behavior
Gap Register.Action to close gap: Generate secure and deliberately transparent lab profiles with known sampling/subscription parameters
Gap Register.Validation evidence required: Pinned security settings; capture visibility limits; publish/sampling rates and application logs

Gap Register.Current evidence / partial coverage: Selected substation corpus establishes GOOSE only
Gap Register.Why it matters: MMS and Sampled Values are different aspects of substation communication
Gap Register.Action to close gap: Add separately documented and licensed MMS / Sampled Values material rather than marking the family fully covered
Gap Register.Validation evidence required: Protocol-level proof, IED configuration, process context and rights

Gap Register.Current evidence / partial coverage: No dedicated safety-system dataset established among the 12 core families
Gap Register.Why it matters: Safety logic, safety state and ordinary process control should not be conflated
Gap Register.Action to close gap: Maintain as a separate future acquisition / simulation track
Gap Register.Validation evidence required: Safety-specific device/state documentation, synthetic safety cases and controlled permissions

Gap Register.Current evidence / partial coverage: Most resources expose packets or tags, not complete operator actions, change tickets and maintenance windows
Gap Register.Why it matters: The same protocol-valid action can be permitted or unauthorized depending on context
Gap Register.Action to close gap: Author benign and unauthorized variants using identical command types with different context
Gap Register.Validation evidence required: Operator event ledger, authority/maintenance context, alarm acknowledgements and device state

Gap Register.Gap within selected corpus: Release integrity, labels and replay-quality checks
Gap Register.Current evidence / partial coverage: WADI label polarity, KNX response labels, IEC baseline CSV and SWaT edition IDs require special treatment
Gap Register.Why it matters: Bad labels or mismatched releases can make an otherwise polished challenge unsound
Gap Register.Action to close gap: Keep file hashes, schema versions, known issues, label semantics, capture metadata and split manifests
Gap Register.Validation evidence required: File-level manifest, checksums, packet completeness, clocks and reproducible answer key

Gap Register.Current evidence / partial coverage: SWaT/WADI restrict onward sharing; HAI has conflicting notices; IEC and S4x15 lack a confirmed broad grant
Gap Register.Why it matters: Publicly downloadable material cannot automatically be placed on an internal or public event server
Gap Register.Action to close gap: Clear rights early; publish only permitted curated datasets and clean self-generated traces
Gap Register.Validation evidence required: Stored license snapshots / grants, attribution bundle and explicit participant access model

Gap Register.Current evidence / partial coverage: 4SICS and S4x15 are 2015 lab collections; newer generators support contemporary experiment design
Gap Register.Why it matters: Historical authenticity should not be mistaken for a current production reference architecture
Gap Register.Action to close gap: Pair historical exercises with a version-pinned modern synthetic plant and explain differences
Gap Register.Validation evidence required: Architecture version, component inventory and explicit scope of what the scenario represents

Glossary.Meaning / handling rule: Supervisory monitoring and control; not necessarily the controller's local control loop.
Control systems used to monitor or operate industrial processes.
Systems interacting with physical processes; not synonymous with ordinary enterprise networking.
Captured packets. PCAPNG means PCAP Next Generation container format.
Controller executing control logic; not automatically a complete process simulator.
Operator interface for status, alarms and permitted commands.
Remote telemetry/control device.
Signals linking controller logic to sensors and actuators.
Industrial control platform; distinct from raw packet data.
Protection/control device, commonly in electrical systems.
Real control hardware coupled to a simulated process or system.
Challenge format; the presence of CTF traffic does not provide complete labels.
Transport used by Modbus TCP and other applications.
Network-layer protocol; some industrial traffic is non-IP Ethernet or fieldbus.
Industrial application protocol used over EtherNet/IP; explicit and implicit traffic are not interchangeable.
Industrial information and service framework; gateway-acquired CSV is not a packet trace.
Utility-oriented telemetry and control protocol.
Standards body; relevant families include IEC 60870-5-104 and IEC 61850.
IEC 61850 event messaging present in the selected substation dataset.
A separate substation communication component; not confirmed by GOOSE-only coverage.
Building-automation protocol family.
Industrial Ethernet protocol family; do not infer coverage from Siemens S7comm.
Building-control standard / brand; the selected capture describes twisted-pair bus telegrams.
Industrial Ethernet fieldbus; listed OpenPLC plugin is not an existing labeled corpus.
Tabular values; may contain sensor data or packet-derived features, not necessarily original packets.
Machine-readable knowledge format; ATT&CK provides STIX 2.1 collections.

Glossary.Meaning / handling rule: NIST SP 800-82 is guidance, not a packet dataset.

Glossary.Term: Adversarial Tactics, Techniques, and Common Knowledge

Software copyleft license; inspect version and obligations for each component.
Different content-license obligations; HAI lists conflicting notices.
Permissive software/content license notice; retain copyright and permission text.
Mechanism used by newer HAI releases to retrieve actual large files.
Measured or simulated process state with provenance. A potentially manipulated sensor value is not an independent oracle.
Qualitative judgment of actual device traffic, implemented protocol behavior and emulation limitations; no numerical benchmark score.
Distinguish real laboratory process, HIL-augmented process, simulation, baseline values and absent physical context.
Beginner: guided discovery; intermediate: protocol/context analysis; advanced: multi-stream causal analysis and modeling.
Low: reference preparation; intermediate: data/label curation; advanced: integration, instrumentation or large synchronized releases. Not a time estimate.
Proposed learning role based on documented strengths and limitations, not a tested event-readiness certification.
Documented generator behavior or capability; must be run and captured before claiming active wire coverage.
Protocol in the documented testbed or collection path; does not prove it is in a distributed PCAP.
Owner explicitly describes protocol traces / uses a protocol-specific filename. Binary QA remains outstanding.
Discovery or configuration evidence only; do not count as validated protocol coverage.
Reference contributes no packet coverage. Dash means not established in this review, not proof of absence.
Primary documentation, license and configuration review only. No full PCAP archive audit, runtime benchmark or permission request was performed.
